Title: Normotopic cortex is the major contributor to epilepsy in experimental double cortex.

Journal/Date: Annals of neurology (2014)

MeSH Keywords: Animals, Bicuculline, Cerebral Cortex, Classical Lissencephalies and Subcortical Band Heterotopias, Convulsants, Disease Models, Animal, Doublecortin Domain Proteins, Doublecortin Protein


--- ABSTRACT ---
[OBJECTIVE]: Subcortical band heterotopia (SBH) is a cortical malformation formed when neocortical neurons prematurely stop their migration in the white matter, forming a heterotopic band below the normotopic cortex, and is generally associated with intractable epilepsy. Although it is clear that the band heterotopia and the overlying cortex both contribute to creating an abnormal circuit prone to generate epileptic discharges, it is less understood which part of this circuitry is the most critical. Here, we sought to identify the origin of epileptiform activity in a targeted genetic model of SBH in rats.
[METHODS]: Rats with SBH (Dcx-KD rats) were generated by knocking down the Dcx gene using shRNA vectors transfected into neocortical progenitors of rat embryos. Origin, spatial extent, and laminar profile of bicuculline-induced interictal-like activity on neocortical slices were analyzed by using extracellular recordings from 60-channel microelectrode arrays. Susceptibility to pentylenetetrazole-induced seizures was assessed by electrocorticography in head-restrained nonanesthetized rats.
[RESULTS]: We show that the band heterotopia does not constitute a primary origin for interictal-like epileptiform activity in vitro and is dispensable for generating induced seizures in vivo. Furthermore, we report that most interictal-like discharges originating in the overlying cortex secondarily propagate to the band heterotopia. Importantly, we found that in vivo suppression of neuronal excitability in SBH does not alter the higher propensity of Dcx-KD rats to display seizures.
[INTERPRETATION]: These results suggest a major role of the normotopic cortex over the band heterotopia in generating interictal epileptiform activity and seizures in brains with SBH.

--- ABSTRACT ---
Subcortical band heterotopia (SBH), also known as double-cortex syndrome, is a neuronal migration disorder characterized by an accumulation of neurons in a heterotopic band below the normotopic cortex. The majority of patients with SBH have mild to moderate intellectual disability and intractable epilepsy. However, it is still not clear how cortical networks are organized in SBH patients and how this abnormal organization contributes to improper brain function. In this study, cortical networks were investigated in the barrel cortex in an animal model of SBH induced by in utero knockdown of Dcx, main causative gene of this condition in human patients. When the SBH was localized below the Barrel Field (BF), layer (L) four projection to correctly positioned L2/3 pyramidal cells was weakened due to lower connectivity. Conversely, when the SBH was below an adjacent cortical region, the excitatory L4 to L2/3 projection was stronger due to increased L4 neuron excitability, synaptic strength and excitation/inhibition ratio of L4 to L2/3 connection. We propose that these developmental alterations contribute to the spectrum of clinical dysfunctions reported in patients with SBH.

key_findings.finding: The strongest direct localization study supports normotopic cortex as the major epileptogenic compartment in experimental double cortex: in Dcx-knockdown rats, 60-channel microarray recordings of bicuculline-treated neocortical slices found the SBH band was not a primary source of interictal-like activity, while most discharges began in overlying normotopic cortex and propagated secondarily into the band. In vivo, the band was dispensable for pentylenetetrazole-induced seizures, and suppressing SBH neuronal excitability did not remove the heightened seizure susceptibility.

source_tools.relevance: Direct experimental localization with multielectrode recordings, in vivo seizure testing, and selective excitability suppression

key_findings.finding: The same Dcx-knockdown model shows that heterotopic cortex is not inert: it participates in an abnormal interconnected circuit and receives propagated normotopic discharges. The balance of circuit abnormalities depends on anatomy; when SBH lies beneath barrel field, L4-to-L2/3 excitation is weakened, whereas when SBH is adjacent, L4 excitability, synaptic strength, and excitation/inhibition ratio are increased, providing a mechanism for network susceptibility without demonstrating primary seizure initiation in the band.

source_tools.relevance: Direct slice circuit physiology and connectivity measurements in Dcx-knockdown rat cortex

key_findings.finding: A bilateral SBH Dcx-knockdown rat model develops spontaneous nonconvulsive spike-wave seizures by about 2 months, with alpha/theta-dominant activity and secondary higher-frequency components; events were more frequent during quiet wakefulness, increased in frequency and duration with age, and were transiently alleviated by ethosuximide. Telemetric ECoG sometimes showed initiation from the hemisphere with the larger SBH, but event frequency/duration did not correlate with SBH size; this provides evidence for bilateral network involvement but is weaker than laminar/microarray localization and does not establish the heterotopic band as the onset site.

source_tools.relevance: Direct chronic bilateral ECoG study with seizure phenomenology and hemispheric onset observations

key_findings.finding: The genetically distinct tish rat (Eml1 deletion; bilateral heterotopic dysplastic cortex) has early spontaneous spike-wave bursts beginning around postnatal day 17, and the mutant allele co-segregates with the dysplastic cortex and early SWD phenotype. However, the available evidence does not localize onset to normotopic versus heterotopic cortex, so it supports epileptogenicity of the overall malformation but not compartment-specific causality.

source_tools.relevance: Direct developmental EEG/genetic-segregation evidence, but no compartment-resolved onset localization

key_findings.finding: Overall conclusion: in experimental SBH/double-cortex models, normotopic cortex is the best-supported major contributor to seizure initiation and interictal epileptiform generation, while heterotopic cortex acts mainly as a participant/propagation target and network-modifying substrate. Evidence for heterotopic initiation is limited to occasional hemisphere-level ECoG observations in bilateral Dcx-SBH rats and cannot distinguish the band from adjacent normotopic tissue; direct imaging or lesion studies proving band-first onset were not identified in the searched animal literature.

source_tools.relevance: Bilateral spontaneous ECoG and onset caveat

entities.name: Experimental double cortex
observations: In Dcx-knockdown rat subcortical band heterotopia, most bicuculline-induced interictal-like discharges began in overlying normotopic cortex and propagated into the heterotopic band; suppressing band excitability did not remove heightened pentylenetetrazole seizure susceptibility.

Bilateral Dcx-knockdown rats developed spontaneous nonconvulsive spike-wave events, demonstrating epileptogenicity of the broader malformation-associated network without proving heterotopic-band onset.
In Eml1-deficient tish rats, early spontaneous spike-wave bursts were associated with bilateral heterotopic dysplastic cortex, but onset was not localized to normotopic versus heterotopic tissue.

source_tools.relevance: Direct compartment localization and in vivo perturbation

entities.name: Normotopic cortex
observations: Best-supported primary epileptogenic compartment in the searched experimental double-cortex literature: most localized interictal-like discharges began here and then propagated into the SBH band.
Dcx-associated heterotopia can remodel normotopic cortical excitability and synaptic excitation/inhibition balance, providing a mechanism for seizure susceptibility.

entities.name: Heterotopic cortex
observations: Participates in an abnormal interconnected circuit and receives propagated normotopic discharges, but was not a primary source in the strongest direct localization study.
Occasional hemisphere-level seizure initiation in bilateral Dcx-SBH rats cannot distinguish heterotopic band from adjacent normotopic tissue; direct band-first onset evidence was not identified.
